title: slot-duration-batcher: adaptive slot packing to minimize padding and kernel churn
author: Diya Patel
release_notes: Introduces Slot Duration Batcher: an opt-in runtime batching strategy that groups in-flight requests into variable-duration slots to reduce padding waste and minimize kernel warp transitions. Enabled via runtime config; no API changes. Improves throughput for mixed-length workloads and reduces per-token cost in common web-chat workloads.
description: Summary: Introduces the Slot Duration Batcher, a new adaptive batching heuristic that packs requests into time-slots sized by predicted sequence-duration rather than fixed seqlen buckets. Motivation: observed pad-waste and frequent kernel-context switches when workloads contained wide variance in sequence lengths; existing bucketing reduces waste but causes kernel churn for marginal length differences and doesn't account for KV cache locality. Design/heuristic: 1) compute light-weight duration estimate for each request using prefix-length, model profile and estimated decode budget; 2) place incoming requests into active slots where the predicted extra padding cost is minimized, preferring slots with similar decode-duration to preserve kernel locality and KV cache reuse; 3) apply soft slot expiration (ms granularity) to avoid latency tail; 4) kernel-hinting: expose per-slot dominant sequence-length to the kernel selection layer so it can pick quantized kernels optimized for that effective seqlen. API/Config: opt-in runtime flag runtime.batch_strategy=slot_duration plus tunables: slot_max_wait_ms, slot_duration_quant, pad_waste_threshold. Implementation notes: added a lightweight slot manager in runtimes/batching with O(1) amortized insert/evict, a kernel-hint propagation path to the scheduler, and KV-cache affinity heuristics to prefer grouping requests that touch overlapping key-ranges. Benchmark summary: - Mixed chat workload (Pareto: 70% short <64, 30% long 256-1024): baseline dynamic bucketing: mean latency 83ms p50 45ms p95 220ms; slot-duration-batcher: mean latency 76ms p50 42ms p95 190ms (-9% mean, -14% p95) and token-cost reduced by ~11% due to pad reduction. - Large-batch throughput test on A100 80GB: sustained throughput improvement +6-9% for heterogeneous sequences. Safety: batch strategy is opt-in; fallbacks to existing bucket-based batcher if slot saturation occurs. Rollout plan: feature gated on dedicated and hosted; start with low-traffic rollout, monitor token-cost and latency SLOs.
